newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast gasolines rise on refinery concerns.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast gasolines rise on refinery concerns.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices rose strongly Thursday, with sellers raising offers in response to slow refinery restarts and a likely strike at four Unocal plants in California, traders said.
The strike, which could start late Sunday or Monday, would not disrupt production if non-union employees continue to run the plant, traders said.
Supply was also lifted by prolonged maintenance at Exxon, Mobil, and Unocal plants, which is expected to end next week.
"Those three refiners are putting pressure on the market," one trader said.
The strike threat emerges as West Coast gasoline stocks dipped to a relatively thin to 25.7 million barrels, down 1.2 million barrels last week .
Offers for CARB gasoline in Los Angeles were talked 2.50 cents gallon higher Thursday at 83 cents, traders said.
Conventional grade rose 0.50 cents to 78/79 cents.
In San Francisco, CARB gasoline rose 1.50 cents a gallon to 80/81 cents on Thursday.
Distillates also found support on the refinery news, with L.A. low sulphur diesel up 1.50 cents to 66/67 cents, and San Francisco assessed two cents lower.
